article.name: Agent Memory Engine
article.summary: A local-first MCP runtime for coding-agent memory and project knowledge. It combines a structured memory tree with indexed source material; source inspection does not establish runtime quality or measured performance.

who_what.text: The upstream project describes a local-first Python runtime for coding-agent memory and project knowledge, exposed primarily over MCP stdio. It also contains a FastAPI interface for direct use; this review does not inspect or measure a deployment.

architecture.text: Memory is represented as a project-scoped tree of MemoryNode records, with staged MemoryCandidate records, relations, and attached evidence. Nodes include status/confidence/importance and optional source, branch, trust, and verification metadata. SQLAlchemy maps these records to SQLite.

The separate knowledge path redacts and chunks source documents, records hashes and source locations, indexes text in FTS5, and can use an optional persistent semantic vector index. In-memory vector search is also present as a fallback. Retrieval fuses memory nodes and source knowledge into one context pack, but the two data models stay distinct.

behavior.text: Write: PostTaskService runs reflection gates, stages proposed candidates, and immediately promotes them. Promotion may create, update, merge, supersede, discard, or mark a conflict for review. Updates replace the existing summary and merge tags; merges append a short new summary; supersession preserves the prior node with a supersedes relation. These are source-observed paths; correction accuracy is unmeasured.

Retrieval: RecallService analyzes task/file/symbol context, scores project nodes, applies relevance and scope checks, then ContextComposer fills typed buckets and emits a signal trace. KnowledgeSearchService combines FTS5 with a vector arm and token trimming; UnifiedContextRetrievalService combines both domains. This does not establish answer quality. The composer’s inspected exclusion list omits needs_review, so that flag alone does not prevent selection in this path.

Deletion and lifecycle: MemoryService.delete_node calls a physical repository delete; ORM relationships cascade attached evidence and relations. Retention archive/compaction and source-validity transitions are non-destructive status changes. Re-indexing marks prior knowledge chunks and derived records stale. No reviewed path establishes end-to-end deletion across every storage/index/backup copy.

Scope: memory and knowledge records include project_id, and retrieval/search are project-filtered. MCP workspace validation rejects mismatching provided context; missing context only warns in compatibility mode unless strict mode is enabled. Constraint scope can be global, repository, branch, module, path, symbol, or task-intent. These mechanisms do not prove user/team authorization or runtime isolation.

Provenance: memory nodes carry optional source path/hash/symbol, branch and commit, trust and verification fields, plus Evidence records. Source-validity checks record invalidated or needs_revalidation states on source changes. Retrieval traces carry ranking and compact-provenance signals; knowledge results retain source location fields. Claim-to-source citation correctness has not been measured.

Efficiency mechanisms include incremental indexing, a five-minute in-process cache keyed by project/query/file/symbol/budget and Git context, token-budgeted composition, and a cap of 50 source-validity checks per recall. The token estimate is character-based; these mechanisms do not constitute measured throughput or latency.

Latency observability is not established: the runtime exposes cache-hit and result/token counts, while the observability package is reserved for future metrics/diagnostics. The unified retrieval function captures a monotonic start time but returns no elapsed-time field; no latency histogram or exported metric was found.

metrics.evidence: Retrieval code and traces exist, but no Agent Memory Engine responses were captured or adjudicated in this project.
Candidate update/merge/supersede paths are present; no correction probes or stale-answer measurements were run.
A service-level physical node delete exists, but no deletion workload tested leakage across knowledge, indexes, backups, or other copies.
Project predicates and optional MCP workspace validation are source-observed; no cross-project isolation probes ran.
Source/evidence fields and retrieval traces exist, but no response claims were captured and adjudicated for support or citations.
Caching and incremental indexing are implementation details. No timing observations or latency metrics were collected for this system.
The runtime reports approximate token estimates; there are no system workload measurements of token use, cost, or storage.
No exported latency instrumentation was found in the reviewed runtime; the observability package is reserved. No workload timing data exists.

limits.text: This review inspects source and documentation at one verified upstream commit. It does not establish production correctness, retrieval quality, availability, scaling, authorization, deletion completeness, or benchmark performance.
Atlas is attributed only for the ordinal roster name and repository locator. Its review prose, capability marks, and UI are not used as findings in this article.
